abstract: Banking Dive (January 15, 2026) reporting on Q4 2025 earnings from big-6 US banks: combined headcount 1.09M at end-December, 10,600 fewer than a year earlier and the lowest total since 2021. Wells Fargo down ~25% from Q2 2020 peak, ending 2025 with ~205,000 employees. Citi CFO Mason confirmed the bank is on track to trim 20,000 jobs by end-2026.
keyFindings: Big-6 US banks combined headcount: 1.09M at end-2025, -10,600 YoY (lowest since 2021)
Wells Fargo: ~205,000 employees at end-2025 (down ~25% since Q2 2020)
Citigroup on track to trim 20,000 jobs by end-2026; expects further decline in 2027+
BofA CEO Moynihan: 'work the headcount through operational excellence and applications of new technologies, including AI'
methodology: Journalistic aggregation of Q4 2025 earnings disclosures across the six largest US banks (JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley).
qualifiers: Headcount decline reflects multiple factors — AI-attributed layoffs, ongoing restructuring (Citi), branch consolidation — not AI alone. Best interpreted as directional signal that AI narratives are entering senior bank leadership's public labor plans.
